policy_title: End the hostile environment and create safe routes to sanctuary
stated: End the hostile environment, abolish the No Recourse to Public Funds condition, and end minimum income requirements for spouses of work visa holders. Establish safe routes for those fleeing persecution, war, or climate disaster, with fast and fair asylum processes and permission to work.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • An end to the hostile environment. • An end to the minimum income requirements for spouses of those holding work visas. Green MPs would campaign to abolish the No Recourse to Public Funds condition. Elected Greens will push for: • The United Kingdom to work with other countries to establish safe routes by which those fleeing persecution, war, or climate disaster may arrive in the country of their choice to make their case without having to risk their lives. • A fast and fair process to assess asylum applications. • Those seeking asylum and protection to be permitted to work while their application is being decided.

bearing_set.reason: Ending the hostile environment, abolishing NRPF, establishing fast and fair asylum processes, and creating safe routes all directly engage civil liberties, equal treatment, due process, and the legal rights framework — the core O9 indicators.
Granting asylum seekers permission to work, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visa holders, directly affects employment access and income security for those groups.

Abolishing No Recourse to Public Funds directly determines whether affected migrants and asylum seekers can access income support, housing benefit, and child benefit — i.e. whether they can afford the essentials.

Safe routes and formal asylum processing carry direct national-security implications: controlled channels allow systematic security screening, whereas irregular routes do not — the policy directly affects border-security architecture.

The hostile environment is a coercion apparatus that co-opts private actors (landlords, employers, banks, NHS) into immigration enforcement; ending it materially reduces state coercion of both migrants and the private sector.

Abolishing NRPF extends public fund entitlements to a previously excluded population (a cost), and safe-route infrastructure requires processing funding; partial offset flows from earlier labour-market entry and tax contributions — a non-trivial net fiscal question.

NRPF holders and asylum seekers are concentrated at the bottom of the income distribution; extending public funds and work rights to them narrows the income gap through a concrete distributional mechanism.

The hostile environment suppresses help-seeking (healthcare, crime reporting) in migrant and mixed communities, damaging institutional trust; ending it plausibly improves inter-community trust and belonging through a documented alienation-reduction mechanism.

membership_note: Policy is genuinely multi-dimensional: it targets immigration enforcement, asylum procedure, and public entitlements simultaneously, generating real and distinct effects across eight fundamentals spanning liberty, equality, work, welfare, security, and fiscal sustainability.
